2.note: auto-approved under the user's no-questions directive; reviewer: circuit clean, 1 P9 BOM-delivery error recorded, 3 warnings

3.note: auto-approved under the no-questions directive; top render reviewed and matches intent; place gate 0 violations, DRC 0 warn / 0 parity

4.note: auto-approved under the no-questions directive. Verify reviewer: 0 errors, 11 warnings, both waiver groups confirmed independently. V1 (stale shunt-C budget) accepted as a documented partial miss on requirement 4; V2-V7 fixed.

decisions.what: Fc = 25 MHz worst case; band DC-25 MHz; spec band 22.5-27.5 MHz
decisions.why: user answered 'up to 25 MHz' mid-run; top of band is the worst case for residual-reactance mismatch

decisions.what: Duty assumed CW 100 percent continuous at 150 W
decisions.why: user left the duty field blank and forbade clarifying questions; CW is the thermally bounding case

decisions.what: Spawn tier substitution: fable roles run on opus for this build
decisions.why: fable 5 returned out-of-usage-credits; playbook allows escalating a tier, never silent downgrade

decisions.what: Board-wide copper clearance set to 0.80 mm
decisions.why: 150W into 50R = 86.6 Vrms / 122.5 Vpeak -> IPC-2221 101-150 V band. Exposed HASL lands take row A6 = 0.80 mm (masked traces would be B4 = 0.40 mm). Board is nearly empty so the strictest row is free; avoids per-item creepage adjudication entirely (LEARNINGS 2026-07-29 check_creepage).

decisions.what: Stackup JLC2313_1.6 (2L, 1.6mm, 1oz HASL); no controlled impedance
decisions.why: only non-upcharge 2-layer stackup modeled; at 25 MHz a 15 mm launch is 0.8 degrees electrical (0.002 lambda) so trace Z0 is irrelevant - the no-controlled-impedance constraint costs nothing

decisions.what: Flange resistor gets an EDGE NOTCH, not an interior window
decisions.why: board_init rejects interior cutouts by design - an inner Edge.Cuts rect silently becomes the board outline (LEARNINGS 2026-07-28 geom/layout). Notch also lets the resistor bolt straight to the heatsink.

decisions.what: Termination element must be rated >= 250 W, not 150 W
decisions.why: P0 arithmetic: a part rated 150 W at 25 C flange derating to zero at 150 C needs Rth_heatsink = 0 C/W to pass 150 W at 25 C ambient - unsatisfiable. A 250 W-at-25C part allows flange 75 C at 150 W -> Rth <= 0.333 C/W, which is a real heatsink. Must be re-derived from the actual datasheet curve at P1.

decisions.what: Match budget: residual series X <= 5.0 ohm (31.9 nH @ 25 MHz) for RL 26 dB
decisions.why: |Gamma| <= 0.0501 at 26 dB. Resistor +/-2% DC tolerance costs only ~0.1 dB, so launch/lead inductance is the entire design problem - drives the notch geometry, the tab bridge and the trimmer range.

decisions.what: BOM cost overrun accepted and reported, not engineered away
decisions.why: qty-5 BOM lands ~4.3x over the $40 cap. The cost is a materials floor (BeO/AlN RF ceramic, >=250W class), not a sourcing failure. Degrading to a 150W part or a wirewound would fail thermal feasibility or the 31.9 nH reactance budget - both hard specs. Report the real number (A8).

decisions.what: +/-5% resistor tolerance rejected as a spec answer; re-check ordered
decisions.why: 'DC resistance 50 ohm +/-2%' is a user-stated hard spec. The ~0.1 dB RL argument is about return loss and is not permission to miss a separately-stated DC spec. If no <=2% part is stocked, select-on-test is the fallback and gets documented as such.

decisions.what: 3 corner mounting holes (board_only NPTH), giving exactly 6 total footprints
decisions.why: Budget is <=4 BOM lines / <=6 placements. Parts are R1+J1+C1 = 3 BOM lines, 3 CPL placements. Mounting holes are board_only so they are not BOM lines (LEARNINGS 2026-07-29: a mounting hole is not a BOM line - fix at the symbol). Capping at 3 holes keeps TOTAL footprints at 6, so the constraint is met under the strict reading too. 3-point mount is also kinematically correct; 2 go at the SMA end where cable torque lands, 1 near the notch so the resistor tab solder joint is not a cantilever anchor.

decisions.what: DC 50 ohm +/-2% met by SELECT-ON-TEST, not by datasheet tolerance
decisions.why: No in-stock >=250W flanged RF termination anywhere clears +/-2%; T50R0's part-number scheme has no tolerance suffix at all, so tighter is pure special-order with no obtainable price. The board-level spec is therefore met at incoming inspection: 4-wire measure each part, accept 49.00-51.00 ohm. Documented in the README with the yield caveat - the datasheet only guarantees +/-5%, so a build of 5 should order spares.

decisions.what: Ship BeO T50R0-250-12X; footprint also fits the AlN TA50R0-300-2X
decisions.why: The AlN twin is dimensionally identical (24.77 x 9.53 x 3.56 mm) but 0 stock at both distributors, and 'in stock' is a hard brief constraint. One footprint serves both, so the AlN part is a documented drop-in when stock returns. BeO toxicity gets a prominent handling warning in the README - do not machine, drill or break the part.

decisions.what: Keep BFC280811339 trimmer; Johanson 5602 recorded as alternate, not adopted
decisions.why: 9 pcs in stock covers a build of 5 and satisfies 'in stock'. The Johanson fixes stock depth but costs 7.1x (+$272 on a build already 4.3x over budget) and is a different package, so it is not a drop-in. Bad value for a stock-depth risk; recorded as the substitute if stock lapses (footprint change required).

decisions.what: Shunt-C tuning cannot correct the resistive term - real limit is R_eff = R + X^2/R
decisions.why: A shunt trimmer only cancels susceptance. Series residual X transforms the port resistance to R + X^2/R, which no amount of trimming undoes. At X=15.7 ohm (100 nH, the 'non-inductive' limit of ordinary bolt-down power resistors) R_eff = 54.9 ohm -> 26.6 dB best case, and a +5% high resistor drops that to 25.5 dB - FAILS the 26 dB spec. This is the quantitative reason an RF-rated low-L termination is mandatory and a cheap 0.1 uH thick-film part cannot substitute.

decisions.what: Required heatsink Rth = 0.633 C/W flange-to-ambient at 150 W / 25 C (0.500 C/W recommended)
decisions.why: Datasheet derating curve (T50R0-250-12X p.1) is 250 W flat to 100 C FLANGE, -5.0 W/C to zero at 150 C. 150 W is permitted at flange 120 C -> Rth = (120-25)/150 = 0.633 C/W. Staying at the 100 percent knee (100 C) needs 0.500 C/W and leaves 100 W of headroom. The curve is defined on flange temperature, so element-to-flange Rth (ABSENT from the datasheet) is not needed to close the requirement.

decisions.what: Interface resistance is a material share of the budget: flange is only 2.36 cm2
decisions.why: A 0.5 C.cm2/W grease joint on a 24.77 x 9.525 mm flange is 0.212 C/W - a third of the whole 0.633 C/W budget. The heatsink itself must therefore be <= 0.42 C/W, not 0.63. Must be stated in the README or the number is misleading.

decisions.what: Resistor mounts OFF-BOARD beside the PCB; no notch. PCB rides on 1.0 mm shims
decisions.why: Tab underside is at 2.667 mm above the flange mounting plane; 1.6 mm PCB + 35 um copper puts top copper at 1.635 mm - a 1.03 mm gap. Three 1.0 mm shim washers lift top copper to 2.635 mm, leaving a 0.032 mm solder gap: an ideal flat lap joint with essentially zero added inductance. A notch clearing the full 24.77 x 9.525 mm flange would leave 2 mm rails on a 30 mm board (fragile), and the flange is 1.575 mm thick so it cannot tuck under a 1.0 mm-raised PCB anyway. Heatsink drilling template goes in the README.

decisions.what: Trimmer C1 goes in shunt at the SMA (port) end, not at the resistor end
decisions.why: The cancelling network is Y_in = jwC + 1/(R + jwL): the shunt susceptance must be at the port side of the series inductance. Trimmer range 3-33 pF at 25 MHz cancels series X from 1.18 to 12.9 ohm = 7.5 to 82 nH. Below 7.5 nH the trimmer's own minimum over-corrects by <0.4 percent reflection (RL > 49 dB), so the low end costs nothing. Shunt C cannot cancel a CAPACITIVE residual - benign here since the residual is inductive by construction.

decisions.what: Board outline fixed at 24.0 x 16.0 mm (43 percent of the 30x30 HARD cap)
decisions.why: 16.0 axis is fully determined: 4.2 J1 pin inset (footprint copper half-extent 3.65 + 0.30 JLC edge rule) + 4.7 to the R1 pad (floor 4.43) + 6.6 lap pad + 0.5 edge. 24.0 axis is set by C1's dia 7.5 body on one side (12.65 min from the RF axis) and the M3 screw-head keepout on the other (8.35 min = 2.2 pad + 0.80 HV + 2.75 head radius + 2.6 hole-to-edge). True minimum is ~21x15; the extra 3x1 mm is deliberate P6 packing margin - the outline is unrecoverable after P5 and JLC prices any 2L board flat below 100x100, so P6 freedom costs zero dollars and zero picohenries.

decisions.what: Launch length 4.7 mm; its FLOOR is 4.43 mm and is set by clearance, not by board size
decisions.why: The R1 lap pad is on the 122.5 Vpeak RF net and must clear J1's own ground pads by 0.80 mm: sqrt((d-2.55)^2 + 0.35^2) >= 1.90 gives d >= 4.42. Shrinking the board cannot shorten the launch. Rot 0 (RF exiting between two ground pads) is optimal; rotating J1 45 deg pushes the floor to 5.5 mm. Relaxing to row B4 (0.40 mm) would buy 0.9 mm = 0.4 nH = 0.06 ohm - not worth reopening a settled decision.

decisions.what: Residual series inductance estimated at 6.9 nH = 1.09 ohm at 25 MHz; RL 32.2 dB at the +5 percent corner
decisions.why: Term budget: 1.2 J1 internal + 0.40 J1 pad + 1.74 trace (3.55 mm at 1.1 mm wide, 0.489 nH/mm) + 1.50 lap pad (7.1 mm at 4.4 mm wide, 0.211 nH/mm) + 1.5 tab/gap/strap loop + 0.6 inside R1. Term F is BOUNDED not guessed: RL>=16 dB to 4 GHz implies X<=16.0 ohm there, so L<=0.64 nH. R_eff = R + X^2/R gives 50.024 at R=50 (RL 73 dB), 51.023 at R=51 (RL 39.9), 52.522 at R=52.5 (RL 32.2). Spec is 26 dB. Failure needs X > 12.1 ohm = 77 nH, i.e. 11x margin. HEADLINE: the board meets 26 dB with the trimmer REMOVED (39.3 dB untuned at R=50); select-on-test buys 7.7 dB while the entire launch inductance costs 0.02 dB.

decisions.what: Launch is deliberately a LOW-Z wide line (4.4 mm, Z0 34 ohm), not 50 ohm; no impedance_ohm declared
decisions.why: At 0.0017 lambda the structure is lumped, so the only figure of merit is L' = Z0*sqrt(eps_eff)/c, which falls monotonically with width: 0.489 nH/mm at 1.1 mm, 0.303 at 2.83 mm (50 ohm), 0.211 at 4.4 mm. A 50 ohm launch would be 30 percent MORE inductive per mm. Extra shunt C lands mostly at the resistor end where it is nearly free. Also closes a trap: rules_gen only solves impedance for DIFFERENTIAL pairs, so a single-ended impedance_ohm would look declared and silently do nothing.

decisions.what: Two soldered copper ground straps bond the R1 flange top to F.Cu lands - the RF return must NOT go via the heatsink
decisions.why: The decided architecture covers the signal tab and is silent on the ground return, which is half the loop. Relying on the bolted flange-to-heatsink joint is quantifiably unsafe: 2.359 cm2 through 25 um of grease at er 5 is a 418 pF capacitor = 15.2 ohm at 25 MHz if the sink is anodised and has no asperity contact, plus a ~60 mm2 detour loop worth 15-25 nH. That is a ~10 dB board whose performance depends on a finish the USER picks. Two 0.3 x 4 x 3 mm straps give ~0.3 nH instead. Sizing constraint: the element covers the flange's central 9.525 mm, so exposed flange top starts 4.76 mm off the tab axis - which is what forces the strap side of the board to 7.0 mm minimum.

decisions.what: C1 ROTOR to GND, stator to RF - binding on P3 pin mapping and P4
decisions.why: requirements s8 F1: the operator turns the trimmer with a hand tool at 122.5 Vpeak while transmitting, and that is the intended use case, not a fault. The rotor is the terminal mechanically continuous with the adjustment screw, so grounding it puts the touched metal at ground potential. Stated fallback if the part does not distinguish the terminals: insulated tuning tool plus a README instruction to tune at reduced drive - declared explicitly, never picked silently.

decisions.what: Both copper layers poured GND (overrides the 2L B.Cu-only default); thermal key deliberately ABSENT
decisions.why: B.Cu is the microstrip return under the launch and is what makes L' 0.21-0.49 nH/mm instead of ~0.8 nH/mm for a wire - it is why the budget closes at 6.9 nH. F.Cu is poured so the flange-bond lands and the C1 return exist without adding a footprint (the placement budget is exactly full at 6). No thermal key: A4 puts all 150 W through the flange off-board, so declaring it would make check_thermal demand via arrays and copper for heat that never enters FR4, and place_anneal's spreading term would fight the mandatory edge placement. The PCB dissipates < 0.25 W total.

decisions.what: ONE schematic sheet - P4 spawns a single schematic agent; nets are /RF (root local label) and GND (global)
decisions.why: 3 electrical parts, 6 footprints, 2 nets. Hierarchy would add sheet-prefix net names and a sheet-symbol layer to a circuit that fits on one line. A root-sheet local label spelled RF is named /RF, which is what every constraints.json entry spells; a hierarchical or global label instead makes check_current, check_creepage, check_return_path, rules_gen's HV and width rules and planes_gen's reference guarantee all silently pass on an empty set. Power symbols stay bare: GND.

decisions.what: Heatsink requirement verified against two real purchasable parts: 0.42 C/W IS reachable in free air, at 300x125x136 mm and 193 USD
decisions.why: Wakefield Thermal Solutions 392-300AB publishes 'Thermal Resistance @ Natural: 0.33 C/W' (DigiKey, 65 in stock, 193.02 USD qty 1, read 2026-08-08) -> Rth_total 0.542 -> P = 625/(1+5*0.542) = 168 W, flange 106 C. Fischer Elektronik SK 88 100 SA (100x100x50 mm extrusion) publishes 1.05 C/W natural (DigiKey, 983 in stock, 11.85 USD) -> 85 W. Bare flange with no heatsink: 6.55 cm2 exposed at h=10-15 W/m2K -> 102-153 C/W -> ~1 W, i.e. 0.7 percent of 150 W, so the README must say the assembly is unusable at rated power without the external sink. CAVEAT: both distributor fields say 'natural convection' but the delta-T/orientation fine print was unreadable (both vendors' PDFs refuse automated fetch), and RS lists the Fischer part at 0.85 K/W against DigiKey's 1.05 - unresolved. Ohmite AH50600V05000FE (1.30 C/W -> 73 W) is the one figure backed by a directly-read manufacturer PDF.

decisions.what: Mounting holes are PLATED, netted to GND via schematic MountingHole_Pad symbols - they are RF circuit, not mechanical
decisions.why: R1's cold end returns through its flange to the heatsink, so the whole 1.732 Arms return is heatsink -> screws -> PCB GND plane -> J1 shell. board_init --mounting-holes emits NPTH board_only holes, which would leave the return path OPEN. Use 3x Mechanical MountingHole_Pad symbols on GND with exclude_from_bom set at the SYMBOL (LEARNINGS 2026-07-29: a mounting hole is not a BOM line). Keeps 6 footprints / 3 BOM lines / 3 CPL placements.

decisions.what: Two of the three mounting screws must flank the R1 lap pad; shims must be METAL
decisions.why: Return-loop area sets the residual inductance. Bonding the ground plane to the heatsink right beside the resistor keeps the loop to roughly 6 mm x 2.6 mm (order 10 nH, ~5 nH with two screws in parallel) instead of running the return the length of the board. The 1.0 mm shim washers are therefore part of the RF circuit and MUST be aluminium or brass - nylon or fibre washers open the return path. Goes in the README as an assembly requirement, not a suggestion.

decisions.what: C1 rotor to GND, stator to RF (adopting the librarian's recommendation)
decisions.why: Grounding the rotor puts the exposed adjustment screw at ground potential. That is both correct RF practice (the tuning tool and the operator's hand do not detune the reading) and a real safety improvement: the intended procedure is tuning while keyed, and the alternative leaves exposed metal at 122.5 Vpeak.

decisions.what: Adopt architect B3: soldered flange ground straps carry the RF return, not the mounting screws
decisions.why: Relying on the bolted flange-to-heatsink joint puts a 418 pF / 15.2 ohm series capacitor in the return at 25 MHz on an anodised sink - anodising is a dielectric, so the return would be open or wildly variable with the finish the user happens to pick. Two copper straps soldered from the silver-plated-copper flange to PCB GND lands make the return deterministic and short. Consequence: the mounting shims no longer need to be conductive, which frees them to be INSULATING and is now the main lever on trimmer temperature.

decisions.what: Outline 24.0 x 16.0 mm (43 percent of the 30x30 cap); launch length floor 4.42 mm
decisions.why: Architect: the 4.7 mm launch is set by the 0.80 mm clearance to J1's own ground pads, so shrinking the board cannot shorten it. Kept 3x1 mm packing margin because the outline is unrecoverable after P5 and JLC prices flat below 100x100.

decisions.what: Accept 2.18 mm guaranteed tab lap; pad 6.6 mm with a measure-and-trim build step
decisions.why: Datasheet gives tab protrusion as 3.18 mm MIN with no maximum, so the guaranteed lap after the mandatory 0.5 mm flange gap and 0.5 mm edge clearance is 2.18 mm, not the 3-5 mm assumed. 6.6 mm2 of lap solder carries 1.732 Arms comfortably; the tab is compliant 0.127 mm copper. Mitigation is a README incoming-inspection step, not a respin.

decisions.what: BOM/CPL accounting confirmed at 3 lines / 3 placements / 6 footprints
decisions.why: Assembly hardware (3 shims, 5 screws, 2 copper straps, grease) is user-supplied mounting hardware, not a PCB placement, and the brief scopes the heatsink and its attachment out of the design. Even the stricter reading that counts the straps as a BOM line gives 4, still inside the <=4 cap.

BFC2808's whole family tops out at +85 C (PTFE sibling) and the PP part at +70 C, against a board that sits at 74-88 C. Chose 5602 over the 8052 because the brief requires a documented tuning PROCEDURE and the 5602's tool is confirmed (Johanson 8764, .130 in shank) while the 8052's is not - worth $3.35 across the build. Also gives a wider documented adjustment range. Cost: trimmer goes $44.42 -> $316.85 per build of 5, now 72 percent of the BOM.

decisions.what: BFC280811339 retained as a documented reduced-duty alternative, not deleted
decisions.why: The +70 C problem only bites at full 150 W CW, and CW is the ORCHESTRATOR's assumption A2 - the user left the duty field blank. If the real application is pulsed at low duty the cheap part is fine and saves $272 per build of 5. Keeping it as a priced, temperature-conditioned alternative puts that lever in the user's hands instead of silently spending their money.

decisions.what: Documented tuning range (Johanson 5602): exact null for residual L = 5.75 to 83.65 nH (X = 0.904 to 13.14 ohm at 25 MHz)
decisions.why: Trimmer 1-30 pF plus 1.3 pF pad parasitic = 2.3-31.3 pF total. Solved from the null condition wC = X/(R^2+X^2), not the L=CR^2 approximation, which is 7 percent optimistic at the top end. Low endpoint reproduces the sim-analyst's independent ngspice result (5.752 nH) to 4 digits. Separately, RL >= 26 dB is met from L = 0 up to ~103 nH, because below the null floor the trimmer over-corrects by only a fraction of a pF.

decisions.what: Failure threshold corrected to X > 12.07 ohm / 76.9 nH at the +5 percent corner
decisions.why: sim-analyst solved R_eff cap = 55.276 ohm for |Gamma| = 0.050119 and read Im{Zin} = 1.3e-6 ohm at the threshold, i.e. perfectly tuned with the residual reflection 100 percent real. The architect's 12.1 ohm is 0.2 percent optimistic - at exactly 12.1 ohm it reads 25.98 dB, marginally under spec. Quote 12.07.

decisions.what: Select-on-test, not launch inductance, is the entire error budget - confirmed by simulation
decisions.why: Corner sweep: a 3x change in inductance (5->15 nH) moves RL by <=0.97 dB at fixed R, while the +5 percent resistance step costs 40.40 dB at fixed L. Worst 16-corner result is 31.90 dB, still 5.9 dB inside spec. This is the quantitative justification for spending the build effort on incoming resistance measurement rather than on layout inductance.

decisions.what: C1 net assignment defined by PHYSICAL terminal: case -> GND, insulated lead -> RF
decisions.why: No Johanson/Knowles document labels rotor vs stator for the 5602, and the librarian's inference chain had an acknowledged internal tension. Defining the netlist by physical terminal dissolves the question: a panel-mount trimmer's case is built to pass through a grounded panel, AND the case is the surface a hand or tool actually brushes. Grounding it makes 'exposed metal at ground potential' true regardless of which plate moves internally. No datasheet fact needed.

decisions.what: Tuning is performed at REDUCED drive or with a VNA, not at 150 W
decisions.why: The brief requires adjustment without desoldering or unbolting - it does not require adjustment at full power, and tuning for minimum reflection is a small-signal measurement that is more accurate at low drive anyway. This removes the live-at-122.5-Vpeak hazard from the normal procedure entirely, leaving the grounded case as defence in depth. Goes in the README procedure as a requirement, not a suggestion.

decisions.what: C1's 6.3 mm plated hole is AT JLC's standard limit (max_hole_diameter_mm 6.3), not beyond it
decisions.why: jlc_capabilities.yaml line 47. Compliant with the no-upcharge constraint, but with zero margin - flagged as a P9 DFM watch item rather than assumed safe.

decisions.what: R1 footprint and symbol reworked to 2 pins (RF tab + GND flange straps)
decisions.why: The first librarian pass built R1 as a single lap pad BEFORE the architect closed the return-path question. Block B3 needs two soldered flange-to-GND strap lands or there is physically nowhere to terminate the RF return, and a 1-pin symbol against a 2-pad footprint would fail P7 parity.

decisions.what: Outline grows from 24.0x16.0 to 26.0x20.0 mm before board_init
decisions.why: As-built R1 lap pad is 7.0 mm vs blocks.md's 6.60 mm assumption, so the 16.00 mm launch axis was 0.40 mm over with zero margin. The outline binds permanently at board_init and there is no shrink step, so the risk is asymmetric: too small costs a full P5-P7 redo, too large costs essentially nothing (JLC prices flat under 100x100, and the launch inductance penalty is ~0.3 nH/mm against an 11x margin). 26x20 is 58 percent of the 30x30 HARD cap and leaves real room for C1's 7.6 mm pad, three M3 holes and 0.80 mm clearances. Extra area is SLACK - placement must still hold J1-to-R1 at the 4.42 mm clearance floor.

decisions.what: Heatsink needs a clearance hole under C1: >=7 mm dia, >=5 mm deep or through
decisions.why: C1's threaded case protrudes 4.75 mm below the PCB (6.35 mm stub minus 1.6 mm board) against 1.00 mm of shim clearance - a 3.75 mm interference. The README already owes a drilling template for the 2 flange bolts and 3 mounting holes, so one more clearance hole is a modest addition. Documented alternative: let the J1/C1 end of the board overhang the heatsink edge, which needs no machining AND lowers C1's temperature - both go in the README.

decisions.what: Canonical layer token is Dwgs.User, never User.Drawings
decisions.why: R1's first-pass footprint used the GUI display alias on 16 items. It round-trips fine through pcbnew and fp_verify never sees it, but kicad-cli REFUSES to load the board (exit 3, no report) - it would have blocked every downstream gate with no diagnostic. Fixed and logged to LEARNINGS.

decisions.what: P5 complete: 26x20 2L JLC2313_1.6, parity 0, 10 rules
decisions.why: board_init parity cleared 3->0 by adding Datasheet/Description properties to the LIBRARY footprints (incl. a local clone of J1's stock footprint) rather than by board surgery - the board was not yet placed or routed so regeneration was free. Root cause confirmed empirically: DRC parity compares only fields present on the schematic symbol INSTANCE, not inherited library defaults.

decisions.what: BLOCKING FOR P9: deliver the BOM from the schematic, not from bom_cpl's pos export
decisions.why: Verified by reading bom_cpl.py: build_bom() iterates the parts list derived from the POS export, so --parts can only attach an LCSC to a ref already there - a footprint with exclude_from_pos_files can never appear. R1 carries that attr (correctly - it is not a machine-placed part), so the delivered BOM would ship with C1 and J1 and NO 50 ohm load resistor. No gate catches this: dfm_check's missing_lcsc only inspects parts already in the pos report. Deliver BOM.csv authored from kicad-cli sch export bom (3 lines) with DigiKey PNs hand-carried, and use bom_cpl only for the CPL.

decisions.what: CPL legitimately contains 2 rows (C1, J1); R1 is documented as not machine-placed
decisions.why: R1's body bolts to the user's heatsink off-board - its only board feature is the tab lap pad, so a CPL 'position' for it would mislead an assembler. Board is hand-built anyway (A5). README states BOM = 3 lines, CPL = 2 placements, both inside the <=4 line / <=6 placement cap.

decisions.what: H2 checkpoint auto-approved on the user's standing delegation
decisions.why: The user instructed: do not ask clarifying questions, make assumptions, record them, and proceed. Schematic reviewer returned 1 error (BOM completeness - a P9 delivery issue, not a circuit defect) and 3 warnings, all recorded with owners. The circuit itself reviewed CLEAN on every axis including the C1 safety property, verified in the committed .kicad_pcb. Proceeding to P6; all findings surface in the final report.

decisions.what: Mounting-hole pad shrunk 6.4 -> 5.0 mm dia; outline stays 26x20
decisions.why: Placement proved the intent geometrically impossible: legality uses pad-BBOX, making R1 a 14.2x7.5 mm solid rect and each M3 hole a 6.9 mm square, so only one hole fits in R1's Y-band. Flanking holes need offset >=10.55 mm but the board allows <=9.50 - short 1.05 mm per side. D<=5.35 closes it; D=5.0 gives a 0.9 mm annular ring on a 3.2 mm drill, well inside fab floors, and was verified legal with zero violations. Footprint swap only - growing the board to 28.1 mm would need a full P5 redo because the outline binds permanently.

decisions.what: OVERRIDING my own no-launch-trade instruction: move J1 to Yj=4.20, launch 4.50 -> 8.45 mm
decisions.why: New information the instruction predates: at the launch floor the SMA coupling nut sweeps to 0.45 mm from C1's body in plan, ~2 mm above the board, on an axis height SCALED OFF A DRAWING and not published by the vendor. A nut that fouls the trimmer makes the board unusable and the tuning requirement unmeetable. Cost is +1.9 nH = 0.03 dB against 6.14 dB of margin and a 12.07 ohm / 76.9 nH failure threshold; it also removes 4 silk warnings. The instruction existed to stop casual spreading, not to override a mechanical conflict.

decisions.what: R1 footprint silk must be repaired: 0.12 mm text vs the 0.15 mm board floor, plus silk-over-copper
decisions.why: All 13 silk warnings belong to R1's own footprint graphics (BOLT CL / FLANGE/TAB CL labels), not to refdes, so place_edit cannot fix them - it needs a footprint edit. drc_routed requires err+warn = 0 at any severity, so these are blocking, not cosmetic.

decisions.what: AMENDS the P2 collinearity decision: J1 sits 2.70 mm west of R1's tab axis
decisions.why: Symmetric flanking holes pin R1's axis to x in [12.65,13.35]. With J1 collinear, C1 only fits rotated 90/270, which needs 11.1 mm of Y and leaves a 0.3 mm window where the M3 head keepout lands 0.64 mm from C1's RF pad - under the 0.80 mm HV floor. Rotating C1 to 180 needs 8.1 mm of Y but forces J1 to x <= 10.40. Cost of the offset is +0.39 mm of trace = +0.12 nH against a 9.5x margin. blocks.md s3.3 and constraints.json._note_edges are superseded by this.

decisions.what: Flanking holes sit 3.87 mm north of the strap lands, not beside them
decisions.why: R1's own BOLT CL footprint silk (glyph top at y 16.695) vetoes anything lower. Benign under the adopted B3 decision because the SOLDERED STRAPS carry the RF return, not the screws - this geometry would only matter under the superseded screw-return assumption.

decisions.what: check_silk treats an UNFILLED rect as solid ink - 5 false positives waived, tool bug logged
decisions.why: check_silk.py builds Polygon(pts).buffer(w2) for any *_rect and ignores the fill token. J1's F.SilkS rect is explicitly (fill no), 0.12 mm stroke. Proof: reported areas are exact whole-pad areas (3.80 mm2 = pi*1.1^2 corner pad; 5.26 vs the 2.3x2.3 centre pad), which only a filled interior produces; and kicad-cli DRC --severity-all reports zero silk findings on the same board while drc_routed passes 0/0 ffailing on warnings too. Deforming a correct stock KiCad footprint to satisfy a checker that mis-parses fill would be the real defect.

decisions.what: Planes set to connect:solid rather than thermal relief
decisions.why: Thermal relief left J1's SE ground leg with 1 spoke against a minimum of 2 (starved_thermal, a hard DRC error), and necking the RF could not fix it - even at the 0.9392 mm floor the surviving channel is 0.18 mm, under the 0.25 mm zone min_thickness. Solid is also electrically correct: J1's legs carry the full 1.732 Arms return and 0.5 mm spokes are exactly the return-path slot that costs more than trace width buys. No thermal argument opposes it - all 150 W is off-board and the PCB dissipates under 0.25 W.

decisions.what: Router stopped flaring deliberately at 7.21 nH instead of minimising further
decisions.why: Flaring harder would push the residual BELOW C1's 5.75 nH exact-null floor, converting the trimmer's weak-but-real downward authority into no demonstrable null at all - i.e. optimising the headline inductance would have broken the brief's operator-adjustable requirement. 7.21 nH keeps a genuine two-sided null and is still 10.7x inside the 76.9 nH failure threshold.

decisions.what: Delivered BOM.csv authored from the schematic; bom_cpl output would have shipped without the load resistor
decisions.why: Verified against the script: build_bom() iterates the POS export, and R1 carries exclude_from_pos_files (correctly - it is not machine-placed), so bom_cpl produced 2 rows with R1 absent and C1 blank (DigiKey-only, and no script reads a DigiKey field). Delivered BOM built from kicad-cli sch export bom: 3 lines, distributor PNs hand-carried, qty-5 pricing, plus the user-supplied hardware list. Validated by parsing the CSV back and asserting all three refs present.

decisions.what: 6 silk strokes at 0.12 mm vs JLC's 0.15 mm minimum: documented, not fixed
decisions.why: Inherited from the stock KiCad SMA footprint. dfm gate PASSES (warning severity). Fixing needs surgery on a routed, gate-clean board plus a full drc_routed/verify/dfm re-gate, to improve legibility of a connector outline whose orientation is already unambiguous from four symmetric ground legs and a centre pin. Regression risk outweighs a cosmetic gain.

decisions.what: PARTIAL MISS on brief requirement 4 accepted and documented: C1 has upward-only authority, no two-sided null
decisions.why: The as-routed launch (15.065 mm of wide trace + a 5x7 mm lap pad) contributes ~4.7 pF of shunt C, not the 1.30 pF the P2 architecture assumed from a 3.55 mm launch. Total 5.7-34.7 pF nulls residual L from 14.28 to 94.38 nH, but the board's own residual is 7.21 nH - BELOW the window - so C1 bottoms out. Confirmed three ways (reviewer, my closed form, and the parallel-plate + C'=0.176 pF/mm estimate). NOT respun: at the low stop the board still measures 39.1 dB nominal / 31.2 dB at the +5 pct corner against a 26 dB spec, and restoring a two-sided null needs ~+7 nH of deliberate meander or a smaller solder lap - degrading the PRIMARY spec and the 1.7 A joint to exercise a secondary feature. Documented in README with the respin offer and its price.

decisions.what: Reverses decision 58's stated rationale for stopping the flare
decisions.why: Decision 58 said the router stopped flaring to stay above C1's null floor. With the parasitic corrected to 4.7 pF that floor is 14.28 nH, not 5.75 nH, so the board was already below it and flaring further would not have changed the outcome. The stopping point remains fine; the REASON recorded for it was wrong and is corrected here rather than left to mislead a later reader.
